facts.fact: FAO's WaPOR page lists Tunisia's agriculture ministry, Institut de l'Olivier, Institut National des Grandes Cultures and the national meteorology institute as project partners, and says the national technical team ran two crop-type data collection campaigns in Jendouba and Kairouan for WaPOR 2 high-resolution (20 m) remote-sensing data.

note: The document covers meteorological use of Meteosat data for flood and drought early warning and states no farming service.

facts.fact: The AssurCereals project, led by the Ecole Nationale d'Ingenieurs de Tunis with the national cartography and remote sensing centre, computed drought indices (SPI-3, SPEI-3, Kv) for cereal growers from weather observations and satellite data, with a closing workshop on 18-19 September 2024.

APNI reports that Tunisia's National Institute of Field Crops (INGC) is developing Sentinel-2 satellite image-based nitrogen uptake models for durum wheat as the basis of the CropSAT decision support system, with research underway to assess its feasibility.

systems.owner: INGC with SLU, INAT and APNI

facts.fact: FAO reports a land cover map of Tunisia made from Sentinel-2 imagery, covering cultivated land, olive trees, date palms and orchards, under the SolaWISe project.
